{\LARGE\bfseries\sffamily\color{AtlasNavy} Ell-p smooth convex optimization with a common minimizer localized in two norms\par}\vspace{5pt}


\textbf{Setting ID.} \texttt{SO\_\allowbreak{}FO\_\allowbreak{}C05\_\allowbreak{}radius\_\allowbreak{}lp\_\allowbreak{}FG}



Single-objective optimization



A globally ell-p smooth convex objective has one minimizer satisfying simultaneous Euclidean and ell-p radius bounds. Queries and outputs are unrestricted in the full space.



\textbf{Status.} Logarithmic gap



\textbf{TASK tags.} solution concept: Objective minimization; task family: Single objective



\textbf{MODEL tags.} convexity: Convex; smoothness: Lipschitz gradient



\textbf{ORACLE tags.} feedback quality: Exact; operation: Function value and gradient; public information: Hidden objects explicitly declared; public information: Public inputs explicitly declared; scalar derivative order: Scalar-function first derivative



\textbf{ALGORITHMS tags.} randomization: Deterministic; randomization: Private randomness allowed; restriction: No additional span restriction explicitly imposed



\textbf{OUTPUT tags.} certificate: No additional output certificate required



\textbf{GUARANTEE tags.} mode: Expectation; mode: Probability; quantifier: Algorithm before instance; randomness: Algorithm private seed



\textbf{RESOURCE tags.} budget: Fixed worst-case budget; measure: N first order



\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{1. Setting specification}


\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Task}


Minimize an unknown convex objective globally on \AtlasInlineMath{\mathbb R^d} using exact function values and full gradients.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Admissible model}


For \AtlasInlineMath{2\le p\le\infty}, \AtlasInlineMath{f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R} is convex and differentiable, and
\AtlasMath{\|\nabla f(x)-\nabla f(y)\|_{p^*}\le L\|x-y\|_p\qquad(x,y\in\mathbb R^d),}
 where \AtlasInlineMath{1/p+1/p^*=1}.



There exists one attained global minimizer \AtlasInlineMath{x^\star} satisfying both \AtlasInlineMath{\|x^\star\|_2\le R_2} and \AtlasInlineMath{\|x^\star\|_p\le R_p}. The two bounds concern the same minimizer. They impose no restriction on queries or outputs.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Oracle interface}


At any finite \AtlasInlineMath{x\in\mathbb R^d}, one query returns \AtlasInlineMath{(f(x),\nabla f(x))} exactly. The public inputs are \AtlasInlineMath{d,p,L,R_2,R_p,\varepsilon} and, for the probability criterion, \AtlasInlineMath{\delta}. The function and a minimizer are hidden.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Output}


Return any measurable point \AtlasInlineMath{\widehat x\in\mathbb R^d} determined by the transcript, possibly unqueried. No value or optimality certificate is required.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Loss or accuracy criterion}


The base loss is \AtlasInlineMath{f(\widehat x)-f^\star}, where \AtlasInlineMath{f^\star=\min_{x\in\mathbb R^d}f(x)}.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Resource accounting}


One exact bundled value-gradient response costs one call, irrespective of its vector dimension. Every execution uses at most the stated budget. Internal exact arithmetic, storage, and computation on received data are uncharged.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Algorithm views and success guarantees}


\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsubsection{Deterministic / Pointwise error}


The algorithm is deterministic and adaptive. Queries, stopping, and the output may use the complete preceding transcript. No span, support, zero-respecting, or memory restriction is imposed.



Internal exact-real computation and storage are uncharged. The stated budget holds on every admissible instance and every response history.




\AtlasMath{\forall f:\ f(\widehat x)-f^\star\le\varepsilon}




The guarantee holds deterministically for every admissible function.



\textbf{Budget convention.} fixed\_worst\_case



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsubsection{Randomized / Expected loss}


Queries, stopping decisions, and the output are measurable functions of the preceding transcript and an instance-independent private random seed. The unknown instance is fixed before the seed is realized. No span, support, zero-respecting, or memory restriction is imposed.



Internal exact-real computation and storage using public inputs and received information are uncharged. The stated budget must hold on every execution path.




\AtlasMath{\forall f:\ \mathbb E[f(\widehat x)-f^\star]\le\varepsilon}




Expectation is over private algorithmic randomization after fixing the objective.



\textbf{Budget convention.} fixed\_worst\_case



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsubsection{Randomized / Failure probability delta}


Queries, stopping decisions, and the output are measurable functions of the preceding transcript and an instance-independent private random seed. The unknown instance is fixed before the seed is realized. No span, support, zero-respecting, or memory restriction is imposed.



Internal exact-real computation and storage using public inputs and received information are uncharged. The stated budget must hold on every execution path.




\AtlasMath{\forall f:\ \Pr(f(\widehat x)-f^\star>\varepsilon)\le\delta}




The requested failure probability is public. One algorithm must satisfy this bound on every admissible objective.



\textbf{Budget convention.} fixed\_worst\_case



\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{2. Notation and parameters}


\AtlasInlineMath{d}: Ambient dimension \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{d\in\mathbb N_{\ge1}}.



\AtlasInlineMath{p}: Smoothness norm exponent \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{2\le p\le\infty}.



\AtlasInlineMath{L}: Global ell-p gradient Lipschitz modulus \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{L>0}.



\AtlasInlineMath{R_2}: Euclidean radius of the common minimizer \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{R_2>0}.



\AtlasInlineMath{R_p}: Ell-p radius of the same minimizer \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{R_p>0}.



\AtlasInlineMath{\varepsilon}: Target objective error \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\varepsilon>0}.



\AtlasInlineMath{\delta}: Failure probability \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{0<\delta\le1/3}.



\AtlasInlineMath{T}: Worst-case full first-order query budget \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{T\in\mathbb N_{\ge0}}.



\AtlasInlineMath{r}: Smaller scalar localization radius \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{r>0}.



\AtlasInlineMath{r=\min\{R_2,R_p\}}



\AtlasInlineMath{H}: Dimension logarithm \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{H>=1}.



\AtlasInlineMath{H=\log(ed)}



\AtlasInlineMath{A}: Euclidean acceleration scale \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{A>0}.



\AtlasInlineMath{A=\sqrt{LR_2^2/\varepsilon}}



\AtlasInlineMath{B}: Ell-p acceleration scale \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{B>0}.



\AtlasInlineMath{B=(LR_p^2/\varepsilon)^{p/(p+2)}}, with exponent \AtlasInlineMath{1} at \AtlasInlineMath{p=\infty}



\AtlasInlineMath{S}: Joint dimension-accuracy scale \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{S>0}.



\AtlasInlineMath{S=\min\{d,A,B\}}
